answer: The prediction markets that matter to a US trader in 2026 are the CFTC-designated exchanges: Kalshi, Polymarket US, Novig and ProphetX, plus event contracts offered inside Robinhood and Crypto.com through regulated exchanges. Sporttrade is a state-licensed sports exchange that works the same way. PredictIt covers politics. Outside the US, Polymarket's international market, SX Bet and predict.fun trade in crypto. Manifold and Metaculus are play-money or no-money forecasting sites. The table below compares all of them.

blocks.p: Liquidity is the big one. Kalshi and Polymarket US are deep on major games and headline events; the sports-only exchanges are deep on what they specialize in; the in-app offerings are thinner. Fee schedules differ in structure (per contract versus commission versus spread) and the difference on a given trade can be a percent or more. Market lists differ: some venues carry player props and multi-leg contracts, others only game outcomes. And state availability differs by venue, because each has its own history of court orders.

blocks.callout: The same game routinely trades at different prices on different venues. A Chiefs contract at 61 cents on one exchange and 58 cents on another is a three-point gap, which is more than most people's handicapping edge.

blocks.p: CFTC-designated venues are legal to operate nationwide and their non-sports contracts are available in all 50 states. Sports contracts are contested by several states; federal appeals courts have split, the CFTC is suing states to assert exclusive jurisdiction, and petitions are pending at the Supreme Court as of November 2026. A few states have court orders restricting sports contracts. Each venue publishes its current state availability.

takeaways: For US traders the list is Kalshi, Polymarket US, Novig and ProphetX, plus event contracts inside Robinhood and Crypto.com.
Sporttrade is a state-licensed exchange with the same mechanics; PredictIt covers politics.
Polymarket international, SX Bet and predict.fun settle in crypto and exclude US customers.
Liquidity, fees, market lists and state availability differ venue by venue.
The same outcome trades at different prices across them, often by several cents.

faq.q: What is the biggest prediction market?
faq.a: Polymarket by global volume, with its international market included. Kalshi is the largest CFTC-designated exchange by US activity. Both are deep on major sports and headline events.

faq.q: Which prediction markets are legal in the US?
faq.a: Kalshi, Polymarket US, Novig, ProphetX and the exchanges behind Robinhood's and Crypto.com's contracts are CFTC-designated. Sporttrade is state-licensed. Sports contracts are restricted in a few states by court order as of November 2026.

faq.q: Which prediction market is best for sports?
faq.a: Kalshi and Polymarket US have the deepest general sports markets; Novig and ProphetX are sports-only and competitive on game lines. The best price moves between them.

faq.q: Can I use Polymarket in the US?
faq.a: Yes, through the Polymarket US app, which runs on a CFTC-designated exchange since January 2026. The international crypto-settled market is not open to US customers.

faq.q: Are there prediction markets without real money?
faq.a: Manifold runs on play money and Metaculus scores forecasts without any money. Both are good for learning how prices behave.
Yes, but not in the price. Expect a few cents per contract, a commission on net winnings, or a spread, depending on the venue; usually under 2% of stake for a round trip.
